_meta.description: 90 day retention for security-relevant datasets (auth, iam, waf, intrusion detection). Longer than operational logs because incident investigation routinely looks back a quarter, and because a breach is often discovered long after it started.
_meta.cold_phase_note: Cold phase drops to zero replicas rather than using the freeze action, which is deprecated in ES 8 and removed in 9. Zero replicas halves the disk cost of 30-90 day data; the trade is that a node loss in that window means restoring from snapshot. Acceptable for data that is read during investigations rather than served to dashboards. A production cluster with a snapshot repository configured would use searchable_snapshot here instead, which is strictly better but needs object storage.

_meta.description: 14 day retention for high-volume operational logs (nginx access, app info). This is the bulk of the byte volume and the least valuable per byte.

3 day retention for events no parser matched. Short on purpose: this stream exists to be alerted on and fixed, not to be stored. A growing count here is a broken parser, and the fix is a pipeline change, not more disk.
